ai.headline: Prince Harry says he wants to mend ties with King Charles and William
ai.summary: Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, has said he hopes to repair his strained relationship with his father, King Charles, and his brother, Prince William. In an interview with GQ magazine conducted in New York, he described family rifts as a common experience many people can relate to, and said reconciling was the most important goal. He also said he has no interest in sympathy, crediting his own therapy and support network for helping him cope with grief after his mother's death.\n\n Harry also explained why his family moved back to the United Kingdom, citing opportunities for the family and the chance for his children, Archie and Lilibet, to attend British schools. The GQ interview was released as the royal family hosted the Sultan of Oman at Windsor Castle for a state visit. A spokesperson for the Sussex household later said his remarks were not aimed at William or any other royal, and were offered in a broader sense.
key_points: Harry told GQ he wants to reconcile with King Charles and Prince William.
He called family disputes a widely relatable issue and said he wants his own to be resolved.
The Sussex spokesperson said the comments were not a swipe at William.
Harry said the family returned to the UK partly so the children could attend British schools.
The GQ interview was published during a state visit by the Sultan of Oman to Windsor Castle.
ai.unknown: Reporting does not show whether Harry and his father or brother have arranged any meeting or talks to repair their relationship.

ai.headline: Week 7 fantasy running back start and sit calls draw attention
ai.summary:
Fantasy football managers are looking up Week 7 start-or-sit advice as the 2026 NFL season reaches its seventh week. Several outlets, including NFL.com, Yahoo Sports, and CBS Sports, have published running back rankings and lineup guidance, and bye weeks and injuries are shaping many roster choices. CBS Sports says Josh Jacobs and Zach Charbonnet are both expected to return from injury and are ranked as flex options, with Jacobs facing Detroit in a game projected to score heavily.

Other notable calls involve backfields in flux. NFL.com says Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr. have been handling New York's carries while Cam Skattebo sits after a benching by coach John Harbaugh, and it advises against starting Skattebo until his role is clearer. Yahoo Sports notes that Saquon Barkley is still recovering from a hamstring injury and may not be available. Outlets also differ on how much to expect from players such as Kenneth Walker, who leads the NFL in rushing yards per game. The available reports do not agree on every player's outlook, so managers are relying on late-week updates.
key_points: NFL.com publishes weekly Start 'Em, Sit 'Em columns, and its Week 7 running back edition includes a Start of the Week and a Sit of the Week.
CBS Sports ranks Josh Jacobs and Zach Charbonnet as high-end flex options, with both projected for roughly 10 to 12 touches in their return.
NFL.com reports Cam Skattebo was limited to six snaps and no touches against New Orleans after a Week 6 benching by John Harbaugh.
Yahoo Sports reports Saquon Barkley is still recovering from a hamstring injury, so his availability is uncertain.
Several teams have running backs on bye in Week 7, including Detroit's opponent group and the Commanders and Bills-related backs noted by CBS Sports, and Omarion Hampton is in a committee.
ai.unknown: It is not yet clear whether Saquon Barkley, Cam Skattebo's role, or other injured running backs will be available for Week 7 games.

ai.headline: Como beat Manchester United 3-0 in Champions League match
ai.summary:
Como defeated Manchester United 3-0 in a Champions League match, according to live coverage from The Guardian. Como's Nico Paz scored twice, with the other goal coming from Douvikas, while United went behind to an early Paz goal in the 2nd minute. The Guardian's live report had Como leading 1-0 at halftime before Douvikas made it 2-0 in the 49th minute and Paz added the third in the 57th.

The result has drawn attention to United's manager, Michael Carrick. Headlines from CBS Sports and FOX Sports framed the match around questions about Carrick's position, and ESPN reported that Cesc Fàbregas called suggestions he could replace Carrick disrespectful. The Guardian's live blog also included fan commentary criticizing the team's performance. Outlet headlines for the match were not all detailed, so the full context of the club's situation is not clear from these sources.
key_points: Como beat Manchester United 3-0 in a Champions League match, per The Guardian's live report.
Nico Paz scored two goals, in the 2nd and 57th minutes.
Douvikas scored Como's second goal in the 49th minute.
Halftime score was 1-0 to Como.
ESPN reported that Cesc Fàbregas called suggestions he could replace Michael Carrick at United disrespectful.
ai.unknown: Sources do not explain Michael Carrick's future at the club or confirm whether any decision about his role has been made.

ai.headline: EA to shut down BioWare, cutting about 400 jobs
ai.summary:
Electronic Arts is closing BioWare, the video game studio known for role-playing series such as Dragon Age and Mass Effect, according to reports from The Verge, Variety, and Bloomberg. The moves are part of a restructuring at the publisher, which is also laying off about 3% of its workforce.

Bloomberg, citing a person familiar with the plans who was not named, reported that the cuts total roughly 400 jobs and include around 50 people at BioWare. Variety's headline indicates the restructuring also involves Respawn and DICE, with those studios set to work on a Star Wars: Battlefront 3 project. The details of that role were given only in the headline, so the full scope is not clear from the available reporting.
key_points: Electronic Arts says it will shut down BioWare, per The Verge, Variety, and Bloomberg.
The publisher plans to cut about 400 jobs, roughly 3% of its staff, according to Bloomberg.
Bloomberg reports about 50 of the cuts are at BioWare; its source asked not to be named.
Variety reports Respawn and DICE will work on Star Wars: Battlefront 3 as part of the restructuring.
ai.unknown: It is not yet clear how the BioWare closure will affect games in the Dragon Age and Mass Effect series, and the full details of the restructuring were not available in the sources reviewed.

ai.headline: Meta reports Q3 results as a New Mexico $25 billion penalty lands
ai.summary:
Interest in Meta stock is rising around two developments that landed on the same day. Meta was scheduled to release its third-quarter results after the market closed on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, the first major report of Big Tech's earnings season. Analysts polled by Bloomberg expected earnings of about $3.56 per share and revenue near $63.3 billion, compared with $1.05 per share and $51.2 billion a year earlier. Capital spending was projected to rise roughly 117% to $41 billion, and Reality Labs was expected to post an operating loss of about $5.2 billion. Investors are watching closely because Meta is one of the largest AI spenders, and Bloomberg reported that a weak result could add to existing worries about the AI trade.

Separately, a New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in penalties, according to a court filing reported by CNBC. The case stems from the Cambridge Analytica scandal and a September jury finding that the company misled state residents about data privacy and the handling of harmful content. The jury counted more than 43 million violations under the state's unfair practices law, with a maximum of $5,000 each, but the judge set the final amount, which was reduced from a much larger figure the filing cited. The judge also said interest would accrue at 15% a year until the fine is paid. CNBC said it had contacted Meta for comment, and the company's response was not reported in the sources reviewed.
key_points: Meta was set to report third-quarter 2026 results after the close on Wednesday, October 21.
Bloomberg analyst consensus expected about $3.56 EPS and $63.3 billion in revenue, versus $1.05 and $51.2 billion a year earlier.
Projected capital expenditures were about $41 billion, up roughly 117% year over year.
A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over privacy and consumer-protection violations, according to CNBC.
The penalty is tied to the Cambridge Analytica scandal; the judge set interest at 15% a year until paid.
ai.unknown: It is not yet clear how Meta will respond to the $25 billion penalty, whether it will appeal, or how the quarterly results will be received by investors.
